q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a chaff cutter?
title: Chaff cutter carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the steel frame, cast flywheel, blades and gears per machine and multiply by supplier figures, adding the motor for electric models. Add cutting, welding, machining and painting energy, then divide the workshop's energy by machines made.
audience: Chaff cutter and farm machinery makers

ul: Steel sections and sheet for the frame.
Hardened steel blades and, for powered models, an electric motor.

p: Report per machine by type and weight. A motorised cutter adds the motor to a hand-operated one.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 12,140 / 400 = 30.4 kg CO2 per unit
Add steel, castings and any motor for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
